Visit note | 2025-11-19 12:00 PM | Dr. Mostafizur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Abdul Karim, 61, male. Mr. Karim presents complaining of lower back pain that eases with rest and stiffness when bending down. He mentions that his discomfort began after moving furniture into a new flat in Bogura. He works as a cricket coach and has no known chronic illnesses. On examination, his pain score is 8/10, BP is 115/74 mmHg, pulse is 75 bpm, and weight is 76 kg. Spinal mobility is mildly restricted with tenderness in the lumbar region, but straight leg raise tests are negative bilaterally. Assessment: Lumbar muscle strain. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to stay gently active, use a warm compress, and lift objects with his knees bent. Follow-up in 2 weeks if the pain continues.

Visit note | 2025-11-19 12:00 PM | Dr. Rokeya Khatun, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Marium Gazi, 30, female. Mrs. Gazi attends for review regarding irregular menstrual cycles and persistent acne on her face and jawline. She notes these symptoms became a concern after a friend in Bogura suggested hormonal testing. She works as a cricket coach and has a known comorbidity of Type 2 diabetes mellitus. On examination, her BMI is 31.2, BP is 120/70 mmHg, pulse is 91 bpm, and weight is 50 kg. Clinical examination confirms mild hirsutism and skin changes consistent with hyperandrogenism. Assessment: Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to aim for a 5% weight loss, exercise for 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up in 3 months.

Visit note | 2025-11-19 12:30 PM | Dr. Mostafizur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Habib Karim, 60, male. He works as a retired civil servant and has no reported comorbidities. On examination, his pain score is 6/10, BP is 114/75 mmHg, pulse is 75 bpm, and weight is 89 kg. He was advised to stay gently active, use a warm compress, and lift with the knees bent. Follow-up in 2 weeks if the pain continues.

Visit note | 2025-11-19 12:30 PM | Dr. Ishrat Jahan, Psychiatry | Patient: Tahsin Gazi, 60, female. Mrs. Gazi attends for a follow-up visit, reporting a persistent lack of interest in her usual activities, low daily energy, and poor sleep quality over recent weeks. She explains that these feelings began after losing her job in Mymensingh. She is a bank officer by profession and has no physical comorbidities. On examination, her PHQ-9 score is 16, BP is 118/82 mmHg, pulse is 72 bpm, and weight is 66 kg. She appears tired with blunted affect but is fully oriented. The patient denies thoughts of self-harm, and a safety plan with the emergency number 999 was discussed. Assessment: Depressive episode. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to keep a daily routine, walk outdoors daily, start counselling sessions, and call 999 or come to the clinic at once if thoughts of self-harm appear. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-11-19 03:00 PM | Dr. Lubna Rahman, Endocrinology | Patient: Liton Gazi, 65, male. On examination, his TSH is 9.7 mIU/L, BP is 136/75 mmHg, pulse is 90 bpm, and weight is 86 kg. Skin is dry to the touch and reflexes show delayed relaxation. Assessment: Hypothyroidism. Visit note | 2025-11-19 03:30 PM | Dr. Kamrul Hasan, Pulmonology | Patient: Saad Bhuiyan, 74, male. Mr. Bhuiyan presents with breathlessness that has worsened over several days, accompanied by a long history of smoking and producing more sputum than usual. He notes his breathing worsened during the dusty dry season in Chattogram. He works as a shopkeeper and has a history of Hypothyroidism. On examination, his SpO2 is 92%, BP is 128/85 mmHg, pulse is 80 bpm, and weight is 71 kg. Chest auscultation reveals diffuse wheezing and prolonged expiration. Assessment: COPD exacerbation. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to stop smoking completely, avoid cooking smoke, and take the yearly flu vaccine. Follow-up in 1 week, sooner if breathing worsens.

Visit note | 2025-11-19 04:00 PM | Dr. Nusrat Jahan, General Medicine | Patient: Tamim Chowdhury, 39, male. Assessment: Viral fever. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to drink plenty of fluids, rest at home for three days, and sponge with lukewarm water if the fever is high. Follow-up in 3 days if the fever does not settle.

Visit note | 2025-11-20 03:00 PM | Dr. Tanvir Ahmed, General Medicine | Patient: Tasnim Shikder, 52, female. Mrs. Shikder presents for review reporting shortness of breath on the stairs, constant tiredness, and looking pale. On examination, her haemoglobin is 9.6 g/dL, BP is 134/70 mmHg, pulse is 71 bpm, and weight is 81 kg. Conjunctivae are pale, and cardiovascular exam is otherwise unremarkable. Visit note | 2025-11-22 11:30 AM | Dr. Mostafizur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Rezaul Islam, 66, male. Mr. Islam visits for a follow-up consultation regarding knee pain on the stairs and a creaking knee. He works as a retired civil servant, and notes his joint discomfort is worse since standing all day at a shop in Mirpur. He has no associated medical comorbidities to report. During the interview, he mentions that stiffness is worst in the early morning but generally loosens up within fifteen minutes of gentle movement. He denies any history of acute knee trauma, locking, giving way, or nighttime rest pain that disrupts his sleep. He reports trying local herbal oils without significant relief. On physical examination today, his vital signs and measurements are recorded as follows: BMI 29.1, BP 128/86 mmHg, pulse 92 bpm, and weight 86 kg. Examination of the lower limbs reveals mild crepitus on active flexion of both knees, with no joint effusion, ligamentous laxity, or localized warmth. Range of motion is slightly restricted at extremes of flexion due to mechanical discomfort, but neurovascular status in the distal extremities remains intact. Assessment: Knee osteoarthritis. A comprehensive management plan was discussed, and a prescription was issued for supportive symptom control. He was advised to do thigh-strengthening exercises daily, actively work on weight reduction, and strictly avoid squatting and sitting cross-legged on the floor to minimize joint stress. Follow-up is scheduled in 6 weeks with ongoing physiotherapy.
